title: 2009 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 9\) and \(CD = 12.\) Diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(E,\) \(AC = 14,\) and \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) have equal areas. What is \(AE?\)

solutions.text:
Since \([AED] = [BEC],\) adding \([CED]\) to both gives \([ACD] = [BCD].\) These share base \(CD,\) so \(A\) and \(B\) are equidistant from line \(CD,\) meaning \(AB \parallel CD.\)

Then \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\) with ratio \(\dfrac{AB}{CD} = \dfrac{9}{12} = \dfrac34,\) so \(\dfrac{AE}{EC} = \dfrac34.\)

With \(AE + EC = AC = 14,\) we get \(AE = \dfrac{3}{7} \cdot 14 = 6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Adding \(\triangle CED\) to each equal-area triangle shows \(\triangle ACD\) and \(\triangle BCD\) have equal areas
Equal areas over the shared base \(CD\) force \(AB \parallel CD,\) making \(\triangle ABE \sim \triangle CDE\)
